title: δM per layer and per sample
question: δM is re-predicted before every SA layer. Does it vary with depth, across scenes, with miscalibration?
result: Per layer it is a fixed rotation: ‖ΔM−I‖ exp 3 200k = 0.70 / 2.66 / 0.29 / 0.28 (CA / SA1 / SA2 / SA3). SA1 is pinned at the predictor's clamp. Across samples ≤ 0.15, cam 0 = cam 1, ≤ 1° change under 60/60, 1–2 of 120 predictor units alive.
conclusion: δM is a learned fixed per-layer transform, not a per-scene or per-camera correction. Re-run at K = 5 after the loader fix: unchanged.

title: What 1b's adaLN signal encodes
question: What does the C-token term of 1b's adaLN carry?
result: Constant at CA/SA0. After SA: shifts modulation by 7–38%, varies 16–35% across samples, 44–71% of that is task. 60/60 moves it by 1–5%.
conclusion: A task and scene cue, not a calibration signal.

title: Attention: external vs wrist cameras
question: Do robust models move attention off the miscalibrated external cameras under 60/60?
result: Every shift is ≤ 2 points; control A shifts as much as anyone. The FPS sampler keeps only 10–19% external tokens, so 80–95% of SA attention is on wrist tokens even with clean cameras.
conclusion: No rerouting. The architecture leans on the wrist cameras by construction.

title: What exp 3's δM does to the RoPE kernel
question: Does δM blur, sharpen or shift attention's dependence on 3D distance?
result: Head RoPE tops out at 1 rad/m (wavelength ≈ 6.3 m). δM acts like a fixed key-side projection; being orthogonal it cannot reduce a miscalibration's positional change (0.340 for every ΔM). SA1 roughly doubles the content-free change.
conclusion: Not a camera correction. The 3D RoPE is very coarse for a ~1 m workspace.

title: Linear probes: camera pose and injected miscalibration
question: Do the C-tokens, δM or the adaLN term know where the camera is, or how wrong its extrinsics are?
result: Camera group: encoder 0.93–0.95, after extractor 0.18–0.23 (chance), random init 0.98. δM and adaLN term: pose ≤ 0.33, miscalibration R² = 0.00. Head C-tokens regain weak miscalibration (R² ≤ 0.22), most in control A.
conclusion: Pose comes from frozen SigLIP and is discarded by the trained extractor. Neither mechanism has the information it would need to correct geometry.

title: Does the prediction follow the miscalibrated cameras?
question: Under 60/60, does the predicted keypose move the way the wrong camera geometry would move it?
result: Following coefficient ≤ 0.007; ≥ 99.7% of predictions stay nearest the true target. With all 4 cameras shifted together they follow (0.6 at 10/10, 0.4 at 60/60).
conclusion: Models use geometry when consistent and side with the calibrated wrists and proprio when the external cameras disagree.

title: Activation patching (history models)
question: Which internal path carries the 60/60 damage to the next-keypose prediction?
result: Share recovered by restoring clean values: scene positions 51% / 18% / 13%, proprio features 45% / 79% / 88% (exp 3 / 1b / A). Clean δM or adaLN term: 0%. Positions + proprio = 100%.
conclusion: The mechanisms carry and fix none of the damage. It flows through scene positions and the proprio encoder (offline, keypose only).

title: TODOs 1 and 3 on the non-history models
question: DeltaM predicts δM from the encoder's own C-tokens. Does its δM vary, and does that explain why it is less robust?
result: DeltaM's C-tokens and δM vary per scene (spread 0.037 / 0.08–0.40) and per camera (2–7°), but don't track 60/60 (≈ 0.6°). Its sampler keeps 30–32% external tokens vs 10–19% for history models.
conclusion: The less robust model has the richer δM. The sampler's external share is the clearest structural difference.

title: Activation patching on the non-history models
question: Do C-token positions carry the extra damage in the non-history models?
result: C-token positions: 0% in both. Wrong scene positions alone cause 51–83% of their damage (12–21% in 1b and A); ~250 samples hurt > 1 cm vs ~60.
conclusion: Non-history heads depend more on precise scene positions (offline; caveat from TODO 13 on cross-family offline comparisons).

title: C-token behaviour
question: How do the C-tokens behave, and are they a damage route?
result: External C-tokens jump ~95 cm under 60/60 but get ~2% of attention; masking them changes error by ≤ 0.02 cm in Base and DeltaM. DeltaM needs their content (+0.74 cm when replaced by the mean) because δM is predicted from it.
conclusion: Generic pooling tokens, not camera summaries, and not the route by which miscalibration hurts.

title: Probes on the full-patch models, inside the extractor
models: FullPatch, rope3d Refine and Direct, random init
question: Do the geometry-aware (rope3d) extractors ever encode the miscalibration before collapsing?
result: Rotation error decodable from late patch tokens (R² 0.47 Refine, 0.60 Direct; 81–82% clean vs miscalibrated) at 1e-4 of token scale; translation never. Lost at the output. Random init carries both at normal scale.
conclusion: The architecture could carry it; training removes it. Downstream all four end up like the pooled models.

title: Full-patch models: C-tokens, δM, attention
models: FP, FP-d8, rope3d Refine and Direct
question: Do the full-patch models behave differently from the pooled ones?
result: δM one fixed matrix per layer with dead predictors in all four; C-tokens constant (Direct passes encoder tokens). Sampler external share 10.5–13%. FP shows almost no offline damage (1.24 → 1.25 cm) yet scores 64.8 at IDLT 60/60.
conclusion: Same as pooled history models. The low external share comes with the history training recipe, not with collapsed C-tokens.

title: Full-patch models: following and patching
models: FP, FP-d8, rope3d Refine and Direct
question: Does seeing patch geometry change following or the damage route?
result: Following ≤ 0.006. Proprio carries 86–93% of position damage; extractor patch xyz and δM carry 0%.
conclusion: Same failure route. Offline keypose damage does not rank online robustness across model families.

title: Exp 4a (pre-LN): attention and C-tokens
question: Does the head use the now-informative C-tokens?
result: C-token spread 0.59–0.72 vs 0; traj→C attention up to 8–11% vs ≤ 4.3%; masking all C-tokens 1.14 → 1.76 cm vs 1.14 → 1.18; masking only external ones: no change.
conclusion: 4a's head relies on its live C-tokens, mainly the wrist ones.

title: Exp 4a (pre-LN): probes
question: Does a live pooled extractor keep pose or miscalibration?
result: Extractor output: camera group 0.57 (exp 3 0.19), task 1.00 (exp 3 0.15); unseen-pose error 47 cm (baseline 50). δM variation is task (0.67–0.77). Miscalibration from δM: R² ≤ 0.01.
conclusion: Scene and task summary, not a pose or miscalibration estimator.

title: Exp 4a (pre-LN): following and patching
question: Does 4a's live δM carry or reduce any of the 60/60 damage?
result: Clean δM replay recovers 0%. Offline 1.14 → 1.57 cm vs 1.14 → 1.81. Following 0.0025 vs 0.0044.
conclusion: A live δM is task-conditioned and still corrects nothing.

title: Online: SBRS checkpoint selection
question: Does the SBRS ladder pick robust checkpoints?
conclusion: No. Retired for checkpoint selection; replaced by the robustness ladder (IDLT calibrated + 60/60, 13 × 20, every 20k from 100k).

title: History extractor collapse
models: every pooled and full-patch history model
question: Does the history extractor pass history information to the head?
result: Every post-LN extractor outputs one constant (norm ≈ 10, identical across samples and all 4 cameras) at 200k, verified on real data. Exp 3 is alive at 30k and dead by 50k. Exp 4a (pre-LN) stays alive (δM spread 0.74 at 120k).
conclusion: History never reached the head in earlier history models. Pre-LN fixes the collapse.
